content.comment_body: Is there any method to retain the date and time in a text message display following a power loss on the [product_name]?
No, this is only possible once the power is restored.

Hello [user_name], There is an alternative solution, though it's more of a workaround than a recommended approach. It does function, however. By using 'Message enable time' and 'Message enable date,' you can display the last recorded time and date of a fault. To achieve this, it's necessary to provide backup power to the [product_name] with a UPS, and a relay is also required. Each time a fault occurs, the input will trigger a change in the message text from 0 to 1, updating the fault time and date. Make sure the program does not execute while the fault persists.
Can you clarify what type of power failure you mean? Is it related to the loss of supply voltage for the [product_name], or is it another voltage source?

analysis.insight_summary: Community members are evaluating how [product_name] devices handle date and time information in custom messages after experiencing power failures. By default, these details are not retained following a power interruption and are only available when power is restored. One user provided a workaround using backup power and additional hardware, but noted it's not a standard or optimal solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] to be able to store and show the precise date and time of the last fault or power loss event, even after being powered off or experiencing a power failure.
